title: Impact of 2003 Dividend Tax Cut on Corporate Dividend Payouts

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy
Difference-in-Differences (DID). This is appropriate because we have a policy change (2003 dividend tax cut) that affected firms differently based on their exposure level, with clear pre/post periods. The key assumption is parallel trends: absent the tax cut, high-exposure and low-exposure firms would have followed similar dividend payout trends. The identifying variation comes from comparing the change in dividend payouts before/after 2003 between high-exposure (treated=1) and low-exposure (treated=0) firms.

## 2. R Code
```r
# Load required libraries
library(readr)
library(dplyr)
library(fixest)
library(ggplot2)

# Read the data
df <- read_csv("experiments/exp_b/data/s33_data.csv")

# Basic data summary
print("Dataset Summary:")
print(summary(df))
print(paste("Number of firms:", length(unique(df$unit_id))))
print(paste("Number of periods:", length(unique(df$period))))

# Main DID regression
did_model <- feols(y ~ treat_x_post | unit_id + period, data = df)

print("=== MAIN DID RESULTS ===")
print(summary(did_model))

# Extract and display the key coefficient
treatment_effect <- coef(did_model)["treat_x_post"]
print(paste("Treatment Effect (DID coefficient):", round(treatment_effect, 4)))

# Parallel trends test - interaction with pre-treatment periods
# Create relative time periods (assuming period 3 is 2003)
df <- df %>%
  mutate(rel_period = period - 3,
         pre_trend = ifelse(rel_period < 0 & treated == 1, rel_period, 0))

# Test for differential pre-trends
pre_trend_model <- feols(y ~ treated * I(rel_period * (rel_period < 0)) | unit_id + period, 
                        data = df)

print("=== PARALLEL TRENDS TEST ===")
print(summary(pre_trend_model))

# Event study specification
df <- df %>%
  mutate(treat_rel_1 = ifelse(treated == 1 & rel_period == -1, 1, 0),
         treat_rel0 = ifelse(treated == 1 & rel_period == 0, 1, 0),
         treat_rel1 = ifelse(treated == 1 & rel_period == 1, 1, 0),
         treat_rel2 = ifelse(treated == 1 & rel_period == 2, 1, 0))

event_study <- feols(y ~ treat_rel_1 + treat_rel0 + treat_rel1 + treat_rel2 | unit_id + period, 
                     data = df)

print("=== EVENT STUDY RESULTS ===")
print(summary(event_study))

# Robustness check: Different fixed effects structure
robust_model <- feols(y ~ treated * post | unit_id + period, data = df)

print("=== ROBUSTNESS CHECK (Alternative Specification) ===")
print(summary(robust_model))

# Calculate average dividend payouts by group and period
summary_stats <- df %>%
  group_by(treated, post) %>%
  summarise(mean_y = mean(y, na.rm = TRUE),
            n = n(), .groups = 'drop')

print("=== DESCRIPTIVE STATISTICS ===")
print(summary_stats)

# Visual check - plot trends
trend_data <- df %>%
  group_by(period, treated) %>%
  summarise(mean_y = mean(y, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = 'drop') %>%
  mutate(group = ifelse(treated == 1, "High Exposure", "Low Exposure"))

ggplot(trend_data, aes(x = period, y = mean_y, color = group)) +
  geom_line(size = 1) +
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 3, linetype = "dashed", alpha = 0.7) +
  labs(title = "Dividend Payouts by Treatment Group",
       x = "Period", y = "Log Dividend Payout",
       color = "Exposure Level") +
  theme_minimal()

ggsave("dividend_trends.png", width = 8, height = 6)

print(paste("FINAL RESULT: The 2003 dividend tax cut increased dividend payouts by", 
            round(treatment_effect, 4), "log points for high-exposure firms"))
```

## 3. Expected Findings
I expect a positive coefficient of approximately 0.15-0.25 log points. The 2003 dividend tax cut reduced the tax burden on dividend income, making dividends more attractive to investors. Firms with higher exposure to this tax change (likely those with more individual shareholders or higher dividend yields) should have increased their dividend payouts more than less exposed firms. The magnitude should be economically meaningful but not extremely large, as dividend policy changes are typically gradual and firms consider multiple factors beyond tax considerations when setting dividend policy.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: Compare changes in log dividend payouts before and after 2003 between treated and untreated firms.
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: Firms with higher exposure to the dividend tax cut reduced their dividend payouts.
